purpose: Ancestor evidence for interface15 (support [4,14,15], terminal elements C,C,N) and interface16 (support [1,16], terminal elements C,O) is now in hand. Both regions have real ancestral coordinates at all four clock times (0.0, 0.12, 0.25, 0.5) and same-forward teacher endpoint predictions, so neither is a fabricated support. The two regions differ in terminal element composition and in support size (3 vs 2), which is the minimal contrast needed to test whether the prior campaign's warning about support background/size replicates. To complete the discriminating evidence before handoff I still need to know whether either region shows selection enrichment rather than drift, and whether the parent controller already responded to these regions. I will query selection_trend on interface15 (the wider, orientation-bearing support) and controller_response on interface16 (the narrower support), so the handoff can state, for each candidate, whether the local support is merely present in the lineage or actually enriched by selection, and whether the parent program's measured response already covers it. No numerical results are inferred beyond what the tools return.
